answer: Each block of content holds attention for a characteristic time — longer for dense text, shorter for images — and the dwell distribution is stable per operator. The network records dwell time per block and flags a session whose dwell times are identical for every block, which means nothing was actually read. Like a copper in a session log, one odd action hides easily, so the check runs on every request rather than a sample. The trellis keeps the process honest and the mirror keeps it open, so challengers can always recheck.
